'''Zhaire Smith''' (born June 4, 1999) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played college basketball for [[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech]].

Smith attended [[Lakeview Centennial High School]], where he was coached by J. T. Locklear. He averaged  20.1 points, 6.6 rebounds and 3.0 assists per game as a senior. Smith earned District 10-6A MVP honors and was voted the best dunker in the Dallas region by area coaches. Coming out of high school, Smith was a three-star recruit and chose Texas Tech over [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Men's Basketball Signs Zhaire Smith to NLI|url=https://texastech.com/news/2017/4/13/mens-basketball-signs-zhaire-smith-to-nli.aspx|website=[[Texas Tech Red Raiders]]|accessdate=May 1, 2018|date=April 13, 2017}}</ref>

In his freshman season at Texas Tech, he averaged 11.3 points and five rebounds per game.<ref name=dauster/> He was an honorable mention Big-12 selection and was named to the conference's All-Defensive team. Alongside [[Keenan Evans]], Smith led Texas Tech to the Elite Eight of the NCAA Tournament, where they lost to eventual champion [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]].<ref name="star-telegram">{{cite news|last1=Dawson|first1=Peter|title=Texas Tech's Zhaire Smith officially signs with Roc Nation Sports, loses college eligbility|url=http://www.star-telegram.com/sports/college/big-12/texas-tech/article210173459.html|accessdate=May 1, 2018|work=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]]|date=April 30, 2018}}</ref> Smith had a career-high 21 points and to go along with eight rebounds, three steals and two assists in a February 7 win over [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Silva|first1=Carlos|title=Smith nets career high 21 points, powers No. 7 Texas Tech to fifth straight win|url=http://www.lubbockonline.com/sports-red-raiders-mens-basketball/sports-red-raiders/sports/2018-02-07/smith-nets-career-high-21|accessdate=May 1, 2018|work=[[Lubbock Avalanche-Journal]]|date=February 7, 2018}}</ref> He flirted with a triple-double with 18 points, nine rebounds and seven assists in a 69-66 victory in the Round of 32 of the NCAA Tournament versus [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]], and posted several highlight-reel dunks.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Silva|first1=Carlos|title=Zhaire Smith puts on show for pro-Texas Tech crowd in Dallas|url=http://www.lubbockonline.com/sports/20180318/zhaire-smith-puts-on-show-for-pro-texas-tech-crowd-in-dallas|accessdate=May 1, 2018|work=[[Lubbock Avalanche-Journal]]|date=March 18, 2018}}</ref>

Following the season, he declared for the [[2018 NBA draft]] without initially hiring an agent.<ref name=dauster>{{cite news|last1=Dauster|first1=Rob|title=Texas Tech star declares for draft without signing with agent|url=http://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2018/04/04/zhaire-smith-declare-nba-draft-texas-tech/|accessdate=May 1, 2018|work=[[NBC Sports]]|date=April 4, 2008}}</ref> In late April it was announced that Smith signed with Roc Nation Sports, thus ending his collegiate eligibility. He is thought to be a first-round pick in the draft.<ref name="star-telegram"/>
